content.intro: Lua is a compact, dynamically typed language designed to be embedded in host applications as well as run by its interpreter. Its small core makes it useful for extending software, but a host may expose only a selected set of APIs.

content_blocks.title: Work through the example
content_blocks.text: Read the small example, predict every output line, then run it locally with a compatible runtime. The module table/return is illustrative; save the file on package.path before calling require. Keep the smallest reproducible case if the observed behavior differs.

content_blocks.code:
-- In a module file, expose a small public interface.
local M = {}
function M.double(n) return n * 2 end
return M
-- A caller can use: local mathx = require("mathx")
content_blocks.expected_output: When a caller prints mathx.double(4), the result is 8.

items.title: Mistake 1
items.text: Confusing Advantages and Limitations of Lua with a similarly named feature in another language or runtime. Fix: follow the version-matched reference and test the smallest example.

items.title: Mistake 2
items.text: Relying on an output order or environment capability that the language/host does not guarantee. Fix: document assumptions and make order/capabilities explicit.

items.title: Mistake 3
items.text: Skipping a boundary test or failing to check error-return values. Fix: test invalid and boundary inputs and inspect failure values.
